newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-AEA keeps acquisitive eye open.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-AEA keeps acquisitive eye open.

text.p: British science and nuclear technology firm AEA Technology Plc will continue to cast an acquisitive eye around the businesses in which it operates, finance director Ray Proctor told Reuters on Thursday.

"The business we are in of science and engineering is tremendously fragmented and there are always opportunities," said Proctor in an interview after the company had announced its fourth acquisition since privatisation last year.
The company bought three businesses last year, in research, software supplies and low-level radioactive material transport.
"We have a growth process which is always scanning the businesses in which we operate for potential."
The latest company to join the fold is Canadian process simulation software company Hyprotech Ltd, which is being bought by AEA for 34 million stg.
This purchase, announced earlier on Thursday, takes AEA's total outlay on acquisitions since it was sold off from the state-owned Atomic Energy Agency to 52 million stg.

Gearing will be lifted in the short term from the 25 percent level announced at the end of the company's financial year on March 31, 1997, although Proctor said this would be driven back down by future profit growth.
AEA said the payment will be partly funded by the placing of 6.4 million new AEA shares at a price of 404p per share. The balance of 8.1 million pounds will be funded from additional borrowings.
By 1029 GMT, shares in AEA had risen a penny to stand at 420p.
